title: Karna gives his armor
hook: the boy grows up worshipping the sun, and one morning a stranger asks him for the armor he was born in
carry: dana: giving, even when it costs
tomorrow: who in the crowd knows Karna?

segments.voice: Yesterday: a charioteer and his wife caught the basket downstream. Vatsalya: the love that raises a child.
screen: `VATSALYA: THE LOVE THAT RAISES A CHILD.`

segments.voice: Every morning the young man stands facing the sun, hands joined, praying, until the sun is high and its heat is on his back. That's Karna, grown. He doesn't know the sun is his father. And the text adds a detail: while he prays, there's nothing he will refuse a Brahmin who asks. Today a stranger comes during that hour, and asks for the one thing Karna was born wearing.
screen: `HE FACES THE SUN EACH MORNING.` → `WHILE HE PRAYS, HE REFUSES NO BRAHMIN.` → `A STRANGER COMES.`

segments.voice: The stranger is dressed as a Brahmin, a priest. But the Mahabharata lets us in on the secret: he's Indra, king of the gods, and the father of Arjuna. Indra knows that as long as Karna wears his armor and earrings, nobody can beat him, so he comes to ask for them as alms. The Adi Parva tells this scene early, beside Karna's birth, though in the story's order it comes years later. In a later book, the sun himself warns Karna in a dream that Indra is coming, and tells him to refuse. Karna answers that he can't. He's vowed to give, and he'd rather lose his life than his name for giving. So the sun tells him: then ask for Indra's dart in return. The Brahmin asks. Karna asks for the dart, a weapon that can kill one enemy, and Indra grants it. Then Karna takes a blade, cuts the armor from his own body and the earrings from his ears, and hands them over. Here's the teaching Hindus hear in it. Dana: giving, one of the oldest duties in Hindu life. The Gita calls the purest gift one given simply because giving is right, at the right time, to someone worthy, expecting nothing back. Karna's gift isn't that pure; he bargains for a weapon, and guards his name. But he keeps his vow at the cost of his own protection. That's why popular tellings call him Daanveer Karna, the hero of giving, even though he'll fight on Duryodhana's side.
screen: `A STRANGER: INDRA IN DISGUISE.` · `THE SUN WARNS HIM IN A DREAM.` · `HE CUTS THE ARMOR FROM HIS BODY.` · `DAANVEER: THE HERO OF GIVING.` · then, large: `DANA: GIVING, EVEN WHEN IT COSTS.`

segments.voice: Karna's day began facing the sun, hands joined. Many Hindus still greet the morning sun, Surya, by pouring a little water toward it, an offering called arghya, often with the Gayatri mantra. Turn toward whatever light is near you. Then choose one small gift you'll give today, time, attention, something you own, and ask nothing back. If you don't pray, skip the water and keep the gift.
Karna's abandonment. The child set adrift grows into a man who gives away even his father's armor, cut from his own body, because someone asked.
Your line: dana, giving, even when it costs. Karna gave the armor he was born in. Tomorrow: who in the crowd knows him?

howItsDone: In Hindu storytelling Karna is remembered as Daanveer, the hero of giving; his gift of the armor to Indra is retold as the measure of keeping one's word to give, whatever it costs.

Brahmin.meaning: a priest, of the priestly class

Indra.meaning: king of the gods, Arjuna's father

Arjuna.meaning: Pandu's third son, the archer, son of Indra

Karna.meaning: Kunti's firstborn, son of the sun, raised by a charioteer

Surya.meaning: the sun, and the sun god, Karna's father

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Karna's worship of the sun; Indra asks for the armor and earrings)
Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Kundalaharana Parva (the sun's warning in a dream; his advice to ask for Indra's dart; Karna gives the armor and earrings)
Bhagavad Gita 17.20 (the sattvic gift: given because giving is right, at the proper place and time, to a worthy person, expecting no return)
Arghya to the rising sun and the Gayatri mantra, common Hindu morning practice, in general
